items.claim: I could use Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim and Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz.
items.reason: The usable parking lots are Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus; Universitaetsplatz had no data in this window.

items.claim: On weekdays, Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz showed the clearest workday shape.
items.reason: FACTS has no usable parking series named Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz; the strongest fitted weekday pattern among usable lots is Ulrichshaus (r_squared 0.787).

items.claim: It was quietest around 03:00 to 05:00, usually close to 34%, and busiest around 11:00, often around 78% to 86%.
items.reason: There is no parking series for Universitätsplatz; the usable lot Ulrichshaus bottoms at 34.4% at 04:00 and peaks at 75.0% at 11:00, not 78% to 86%.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Friedensplatz followed a similar shape: very low around 03:00 to 05:00 at 4.4% to 7.0%, then fullest in late morning, often between about 58% and 83.3%.
items.reason: FACTS gives Friedensplatz a trough of 6.5% at 03:00 and a weekday peak of 58.1% at 12:00; 4.4%, 7.0% and 83.3% are not values in FACTS.

items.claim: Weekend behaviour was very different between lots.
items.reason: The pooled test says weekend effects differ between parking lots.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz was usually less full on weekend late mornings than on weekdays: many weekday 10:00 to 12:00 values were in the mid-70s to mid-80s, while Saturday 19 September reached only 45.8% at 10:00 and 49.6% at 12:00, and Sunday 20 September stayed around 36.5% to 38.2% from 11:00 to 13:00.
items.reason: Universitaetsplatz is excluded for no data, and the dated hourly values 45.8%, 49.6%, 36.5% and 38.2% are not in FACTS.

items.claim: Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz showed the opposite pattern.
items.reason: Elbauenpark's weekend effect is +6.8 points, but FACTS marks it not significant, so there is no supported opposite pattern.

items.claim: Many weekday late mornings sat roughly between 28% and 52%, but it reached 97.8% on Saturday 19 September at 11:00 and 98.6% on Sunday 20 September at 11:00.
items.reason: FACTS gives only aggregated values such as a weekday peak of 38.4% at 11:00 and a monthly max of 100.0%, not those dated 97.8% and 98.6% readings.

items.claim: Compared with August, I did not see a clear month-to-month change at Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz or Tiefgarage Universitätsplatz.
items.reason: Friedensplatz was significantly higher month on month, while Universitaetsplatz was not modelled in either month.

items.claim: Their weekday shapes stayed broadly the same.
items.reason: FACTS shows Friedensplatz had a significant positive adjusted shift and Universitaetsplatz was not modelled, so this grouped claim is not supported.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim changed the most inside September itself: it was still at 88.0% on 9 September at 11:00, but dropped to 0.0% on 20 September at 11:00 and then stayed mostly below 30% for several days before rising again late in the month.
items.reason: FACTS only gives Hotel Maritim's monthly min/max and typical peak/trough, not the dated 11:00 readings or the claimed several-day run below 30%.

items.claim: I could use 16 stations reliably this month.
items.reason: FACTS lists 17 usable EV charging stations this month, with 1 excluded.

items.claim: Occupancy was lowest around 03:00, rose from the morning onward, and was busiest around 11:00.
items.reason: The median weekday profile bottoms at 03:00 and peaks at 11:00, rising through the morning.

items.claim: After about 20:00, usage eased again.
items.reason: The median weekday profile declines after 20:00, from 24.7 at 20:00 to 6.9 by 23:00.

items.claim: Weekends were flatter, with more mixed daytime use and some stations carrying occupancy further into the night.
items.reason: FACTS gives per-station weekend effects but no weekend hourly profile to verify flatter or later-night use.

items.claim: Hegelstraße 4 was occupied for long stretches, often at 50% or 100%, including many night hours.
items.reason: FACTS shows mean 53.9%, full occupancy 34.5% of known time, a 05:00 trough of 37.8%, and max 100.0%, but not 'often at 50%' or 'long stretches'.

items.claim: Breiter Weg 203 was often full in daytime.
items.reason: FACTS shows a 10:00 peak of 62.6% and full occupancy 19.7% of known time, but not that it was often full specifically in daytime.

items.claim: Liebknechtstraße 37 also had many very busy weekday daytime and evening hours, including repeated 100% readings.
items.reason: FACTS shows mean 29.7%, a 12:00 peak of 44.9%, max 100.0%, and full occupancy 15.3% of known time, but not repeated 100% readings or many very busy daytime and evening hours.

items.claim: Against August, I did not see a clear overall change in the network at comparable weekday and weekend hours.
items.reason: FACTS provides month-on-month comparisons by station, but no single network-wide overall change measure.

items.claim: The daily shape looked much the same.
items.reason: FACTS does not provide a family-wide August weekday profile to compare with September's shape.

items.claim: I could use all 4 NO2 sensors and the West O3 sensor.
items.reason: All 4 NO2 sensors are usable, and West is the only usable O3 sensor.

items.claim: For NO2, the typical weekday pattern was lowest around 04:00 to 05:00 and highest around 08:00 to 10:00, with another rise later in the day at the roadside sites.
items.reason: The family NO2 weekday profile bottoms at 04:00 and peaks at 21:00, while the individual site peaks are 17:00, 22:00, 20:00 and 08:00.

items.claim: Weekends were generally less polluted than weekdays, especially in the morning.
items.reason: Only Guericke Strasse and Schleinufer have significant weekend reductions; City Tunnel and West do not, and morning-specific weekend patterns are not reported.

items.claim: At Schleinufer, many weekday 07:00 to 09:00 values were around 30 to 45, while several weekend mornings stayed in single digits or the low teens.
items.reason: FACTS do not provide Schleinufer weekday/weekend hour-by-hour NO2 values or the 07:00–09:00 ranges stated.

items.claim: I did not see any NO2 breach of the EU hourly limit of 200.
items.reason: All four NO2 sites had 0 hours above the EU hourly limit of 200.

items.claim: The highest hourly value was 118 at City Tunnel on 28 September at 18:00.
items.reason: City Tunnel reached 118 on 2026-09-28 18:00, and the other NO2 maxima were lower.

items.claim: For the WHO daily-mean guideline of 25, I saw exceedances on several days at City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse and Schleinufer.
items.reason: Those three sites had WHO daily-guideline exceedance days: 11, 8 and 11 respectively.

items.claim: At West, I did not see a daily mean above 25.
items.reason: West had 1 day above 25, with a worst daily mean of 26.1.

items.claim: For ozone at West, the highest hourly value was 120 on 28 September at 18:00.
items.reason: FACTS give the hourly maximum as 120, but the reported timestamp is for the 8-hour mean, not the hourly maximum.

items.claim: The EU 8-hour target of 120 was not exceeded.
items.reason: West had 0 days above the EU 8-hour target of 120.

items.claim: The WHO 8-hour guideline of 100 was exceeded on 27 September and 30 September.
items.reason: FACTS show 4 WHO 8-hour exceedance days and the worst on 2026-09-29, but not exceedances specifically on 27 or 30 September.

items.claim: Compared with August, high-ozone periods were less frequent: August had several 8-hour periods above 120, while September had none.
items.reason: FACTS show September ozone was significantly lower and had 0 EU 8-hour target exceedance days, but they do not report August 8-hour exceedance counts.

items.claim: I could not give a reliable PM10 or PM2.5 picture this month.
items.reason: Both PM10 and PM2.5 have no usable series this month.
